WarMonitor This doesn't look like transparency. It looks like an administration that's afraid of being held accountable. NEWS: In a new letter, White House Counsel Will Scharf told congressional Democrats on Wednesday that the Trump administration is under no obligation to comply with their demands for documents and information, arguing that requests from ranking minority members lack the legal authority of formal congressional oversight. Scharf also said requests made during the current Congress would not carry over when Democrats assume committee chairmanships in January. He said the administration would work with incoming committee chairs but warned that any future requests would face scrutiny over their legal authority and legislative purpose. The letter comes as Representative Robert Garcia, the Democrat expected to chair the House Oversight Committee in January, sent letters Wednesday morning to 12 Trump family members, allies and current and former administration officials, directing them to preserve documents ahead of planned investigations into alleged Trump family corruption, the administration’s immigration crackdown and its handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files. Recipients included Vice President JD Vance, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, Attorney General Todd Blanche and former Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. - Nandita Bose tweet
